correctness.rationale: Conditioning on coverage creates three independent interval classes. Exact pairwise conditional overlap probabilities yield the quadratic regression and the unique midpoint zero second difference. Vertex-edge incidence and the exact integral E[g^2]=22/45 establish covariance and variance. Strictly increasing c^3/(1-c) yields unique maximum and the 5/8 limit. The standalone rational checker passed 522 assertions, but finite checks are not used to justify universal quantifiers.

originality.rationale: A finite-sample conditional expectation for total graph edges as a function of point-coverage count, unique affine location, and exact 5/8 limiting prediction fraction were not found in the inspected primary full texts or searchable published mathematical records. Scheinerman (1988) and subsequent works establish edge density and midpoint coverage maximum; these do not imply the full conditional polynomial merely from their stated conclusions. The original 1988 article remained inaccessible and absolute historical priority is not certified.

value.rationale: Point coverage is a natural clique measurement, whereas total edges measure graph-wide intersections. The exact regression uniquely linearizes at the distinguished median, where knowing just one local depth explains 5/8 of all global edge-count variance asymptotically; this quantitative local-to-global relation is not a marginal-probability restatement and provides a fully classified optimal measurement location.
